ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.

NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

None.

David Ott, City Manager

Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that there was no reportable action for Closed Session.
FLAG SALUTE:
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director, led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Roberts to approve except for Item D.4. (pulled from the agenda) and moving C.4. to the Consent calendar.
Motion carried unanimously.
PROCLAMATIONS:
Mayor Nichols presented a proclamation to Stacy Williams of the American Cancer Society and Dave Carroll of the Chamber of Commerce.
PRESENTATIONS:
(Ceremonial items that do not contain in-depth discussion and no action/direction.)
Mayor Nichols presented an award from the Sierra Club for honorable mention for a Cool City to Wende Protzman, Deputy City Manager, and Steven Goetsch and Roger Boyd of the Clean and Green Committee. He stated that the Clean and Green Committee had worked to reduce the City’s carbon footprint.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today’s agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Comments relating to items on this evening’s agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Council may refer items to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES (SBMC 2.04.190). Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
Roger Boyd stated he had concerns about safety issues at the new I-5 Lomas Santa Fe interchange, that a volunteer safety group of citizens had been formed who identified 15 safety issues regarding the interchange. He stated that the freeway interchange at Lomas Santa Fe was unsafe for pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles, that all users of Lomas Santa Fe had to be aware of the safety issues, that red light cameras should be installed at the area intersections, that placing the "red light" signs for Lomas Santa Fe and Solana Hills earlier on Lomas Santa Fee this would give drivers an early warning as they entered the City, and that the "Safer Solana Beach" group was open to all citizens to participate.
Doug Alden stated that the City should seek remedies for the safety issues at I-5 and Lomas Santa Fe, that he had sent Caltrans letters regarding his safety concerns, and that Caltrans should be invited to a Council meeting to address the public on the safety issues. He stated that the westbound bike lane should be moved from behind the pillars to the previous location south of the pillars, that the yield signs to cyclist and pedestrians should be moved to the first pillar in the tunnel, that the overhead light intensity along the bike lane in the tunnel during day light hours should be increased, that the yellow signal light should be lengthened to allow more time to cross the Lomas Santa Fe intersection, that the north and south entrance ramps should be made "no turn on red" and that the speed limit on Lomas Santa Fe should be reduced to 30 miles.
Steve Goetsch stated many residents had concerns about the safety issues of the new Lomas Santa Fe at I-5 intersection, that the new pattern of off and on ramps were unsafe, that concrete lane dividers on west and eastbound Lomas Santa Fe were needed, that the City should petition SANDAG for funds that were allocated for the interchange project to hire safety engineers to evaluate the area, and that the City had a responsibility for the intersection.
Mary Jane Boyd stated that she shared the safety concerns of the previous speakers, that she had near miss accidents traveling west on Lomas Santa Fe, that she had several incidents with cyclists in the tunnel, and that drivers needed to be able to track cyclists in the tunnel. She stated that the interchange placed walkers, cyclists, and drivers at risk when crossing the street or getting on and off the freeway, that having multiple entities involved in the interchange project made it easy to pass off concerns to each other, whether the City was addressing these issues, whether there were funds and a plan for these issues, and requested that this item be placed on a future agenda to address the public and provide information.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the City did not have authority over the Lomas Santa Fe intersection or the area under the freeway, that various Councilmembers had met with Caltrans to address several issues, and that other safety issues involved crosswalks. He stated that Caltrans would work on some of the crosswalk issues over the summer, that Council had been working with Caltrans on the bike lane under the bridge, and that Caltrans agreed to add a curved barrier before moving over to enter the freeway to allow time for drivers to identify cyclists.
Council discussion ensued regarding their work with Caltrans, that the issue was important to Council, that Caltrans should come to a Council meeting or a public workshop to address the public, that the citizen’s safety group should provide a document to the City outlining their concerns to present to Caltrans, and that some actions were being taken over the next couple months.
Susan Haskell stated that there was a community health fair event at Scripps Encinitas, that there would be several types of screenings such as glucose, cholesterol, and body fat screenings, and that there would be information provided on different health care topics.

(Ceremonial items that do not contain in-depth discussion and no action/direction.)
1.
211 San Diego
Ms. Jimenez presented an update on the San Diego 2-1-1 program. She stated that the organization was growing and she distributed a flyer to council on the program. She stated that the program provided information on community health and emergency services, that the program identified needs in the community, had over 5,000 resources listed on their website, provided services in over 150 languages, and that the community was supportive of the 2-1-1 program.
Council discussion ensued regarding their support of the 2-1-1 program.

C.2.
Introduce (1st Reading) Ordinance 403 - Related to Smoking and Tobacco, Tobacco Retailer Licensing, and Public Property and Places. (File 0270-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Introduce Ordinance 403 amending Chapter 6.16 of Title 6 of the SBMC to provide for the prohibition of smoking in outdoor dining areas, bars, playgrounds and tot lots, and farmer's markets as well as to update the chapter and reduce accessibility of tobacco products to minors; adding Chapter 6.17 to Title 6 of the SBMC to provide for the licensure of tobacco retailers in Solana Beach for regulatory purposes; and amending Chapter 11.12. of Title 11 of the SBMC to ban smoking within the boundaries of the Coastal Rail Trail.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Wende Protzman, Deputy City Manager, presented a powerpoint reviewing requiring licensing throughout the City to sell tobacco and expanding the smoking ban to certain areas.
Councilmember Heebner suggested including street fairs in the ordinance.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that it would be acceptable and proposed to define them as a gathering of people to display, sell, or trade produce or other goods usually held on the main street of a neighborhood or in some other designated public place such as a park or parking lot in which its main component was booths or stands used sell goods or convey information, and that a street fair may also include carnival rides, parades, live music or dances.
SPEAKERS
John Cavanaugh stated that he commended Council for considering the ban, that the cab drivers affect his neighbors and tenants, that he picked up 589 cigarette butts along a span of about three parked cars, that he was concerned that it stated the ban affected the waiting area of the public transit area which there were 3 spaces designated and that there are many more cabs waiting waiting in the surrounding area, and to consider adding the ban to the sidewalk or in the car.
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding another proposal coming forward to curb the butt littering problem and the stormwater issue, consideration to give them notice, that code enforcement had been there several times already but that it was difficult to catch them during the violation.
Kathleen Sullivan, policy manager for American Lung Association, commended Council on the ban and said that it was a matter of modeling healthy behavior as well as benefiting the public’s health. She said that one of the frontiers of tobacco control was outdoor smoking and that she would suggest considering adding entry ways to the ordinance since there were issues with people smoking near businesses and meetings, that another frontier emerging was regarding multi-unit housing and some communities were looking at taking steps in this area, and the third was youth access which the ordinance addressed.
Robyn Wallace, American Cancer Society, said that it was important to protect the public from second hand smoke exposure. She said that the City would be considering an ordinance to prohibit smoking in outdoor dining areas, bars, playgrounds, farmers markets, tot lots, and the Coastal Rail Trail. She said that keeping the products out of the the hands of children was of the highest importance.
Barbara Gordon said that a recent survey performed by the youth of San Dieguito Alliance in Solana Beach on their outdoor related to smoking, that 85% said they were bothered by cigarette smoke when eating outside, 76 of the 100 people surveyed agreed that people should not be allowed to smoke when eating outside, and shared other results that stated that there were not smoke free outdoor eating areas, that they observed restaurants in the area and cited results of outdoor smoking options among them, and that overall California voters are supportive of restricting outdoor smoking among restaurants.
Judy Strang, San Dieguito Drug Alliance, stated that Solana Beach was already on a list of smoke free proud, that the bans had helped people with a healthy lifestyle, and whether the ban would include the Fiesta del Sol.
Robert Wilson asked why the City would be doing this since the state would be doing something similar.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, said that it would be a local program and there may be a violation fee in the future once a study was completed.
Robert Wilson continued said that he agreed with 99% of it, that he would suggest caution if considering the streets since the ACLU went against Del Mar on it, and that would thought the ban would hurt some restaurants that have a separate area for smoking.
Nancy Logan stated that she was representing the 9th District PTA and supported the ban.
Council and Staff discussed adding prohibtion at the entryway within 20 feet, striking the Whereas that Ms. Strang mentioned that may be incorrect, providing education to the community about the ban, and that Solana Beach was the first in the U.S. to ban smoking on the beach.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian with modifications including removing the one Whereas statement and adding entryways.
Motion carried unanimously.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, read the ordinance title.
C.6.
Introduce (1st Reading) Ordinance 407 -Extensions of Project Approvals. (File 0600-05)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Make a finding that the proposed amendments to SBMC 17.72.110 is consistent with the general plan and would not be detrimental to the public interest, health, safety, convenience, or welfare of the city.
2.
Introduce Ordinance 407 amending SBMC section 17.72.110, all related to extensions of project approvals.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Tina Christiansen, Community Development Dir., presented a powerpoint.
Robert Fleet stated that he was a case study for what the ordinance would benefit. He said that he moved from Del Mar to Solana Beach and was given a Structure Development Permit in 2008, that due to the economy and credit crisis he was not comfortable building at the time so he held on and since he was still not comfortable he was concerned about the permit expiring.
Bridget Augusta said that she and her husband had a financial economic issue that had prevented them from going forward and had some investment so far, that they had the intention of building but did not know how things would end up, that they would like the opportunity to obtain an extension to go forward, and that she hoped Council would embrace it.
Council and Staff discussed how to handle if the applicants are on the final days, whether Council wanted more flexibility, that Staff was not currently turning applicants away if they were late and there were special circumstances, what would happen if they missed their deadline for filing, that it was drafted as a "shall" which would take away any flexibility, to consider providing the flexibility due to the certain circumstances and the current economic times, and that if the word "shall" was used then notification should be done by certified mail.
Councilmember Campbell stated that if there is not a definite determiner then the City Manager is put in a position to make a discretionary decision, that if the applicant comes in on day 59 and does not have all the paperwork that they would agree to five days to bring in the final paperwork, and that the applicant is provided the provisions of the terms at the time they receives their permit.
SPEAKERS
Gary Martin said he suggested using "shall" and then providing 15 days for follow up to complete the application including what was required by the department.
Mayor Nichols said that the City should not be in the business of noticing people, that applicants get two years, and that it was their responsibility to follow the provisions of the permit.
Councilmember Heebner said she could agree as long as it was clear at the counter when the permit was issued and that Staff require the applicant to initial that area where it stated the deadline.
Tina Christiansen, Community Development Dir., said that it was in the letter of approval and it was very clear.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that the changes included a provision filed at least 60 days prior to the expiration of the approval and that an additional 15 days would be provided for completion.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, read the title of the ordinance.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Heebner with modifications.
Motion carried unanimously.
